title: The Tale of the Anklet
body: Kannagi and her husband Kovalan lived in Puhar, the prosperous capital city of the Chola kingdom. Kovalan lost all his wealth over a dancer, but realising his mistake he returned to Kannagi, who forgave him. The couple travelled to Madurai, the capital of the Pandya kingdom, to start a new life. Kannagi gave Kovalan one of her anklets to sell, but he was falsely accused of theft and executed on the orders of the Pandya king. Kannagi proved his innocence by showing her second anklet. The king, realising his mistake, died of shock. Kannagi then cursed Madurai, and the god of fire destroyed the city. She walked west to the Chera kingdom, where she was honoured as a goddess. She is still worshipped in Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

title: A visit to the museum gallery
body: Meera visits a museum gallery of sculptures from the Kushana period. The first sculpture she sees is a Buddha carved in grey-black schist stone. It shows realistic anatomy, wavy hair and a robe falling in deep, flowing folds, much like Greco-Roman statues she has seen in books. The second sculpture is a figure of Kubera, the god of wealth, carved in red sandstone. It has a full, rounded body with smooth modelling and a prominent moustache. The label says it was found near present-day Uttar Pradesh. Meera notes that both sculptures were made in the same empire but look very different from each other.
